title: New Residential Construction (Building Permits, Housing Starts, Completions — October 2026 data) — the same reference month as the 11-12 EHS print, on the vintage day 11-12 does not have
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes), row "New Residential Construction (Building Permits, Housing Starts, and Housing Completions) | November 18, 2026 | 8:30 AM | October 2026", release code A202611180830, reference A202610. Corroborated by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet (fetched direct 2026-09-06 from the live path www.atlantafed.org/-/media/Project/Atlanta/FRBA/Documents/cqer/researchcq/gdpnow/), whose 2026-11-18 08:30 row reads "Housing starts". Filed `estimate` per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an in-sweep discovery, and doubly so because the same Census page demonstrably carries `Suspended` rows. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06). Why it earns its own row rather than a line in that ledger: it is the only way to read the OTHER half of the residential picture for the same reference month. The 11-12 EHS print reports October closings and the Atlanta Fed schedules no GDPNow vintage that day at all (verified against the full 82-row PostedUpdates sheet, 2025-12-23 -> 2026-12-23), so October's residential story reaches the nowcast only here, six days later, on a day the model DOES post. The workbook's Residential sheet routes `valExHomeSales` into `FRSBKX_USNAqtr` ("Brokerage commissions") and `SplicedNewHousingConstruction` into `FRSPX_USNAqtr` ("Permanent-site" construction) — the far larger leaf. So 11-12 is the month's tape-readable half and 11-18 is its nowcast-readable half, which is a cleaner separation than the corridor has anywhere else. Note for whoever picks this up, because it is the mirror of what makes 11-12 the control: 11-18 is itself confounded on the axis 11-12 is clean on — the FOMC minutes of the Oct 27-28 meeting land 14:00 that same day (fomc-minutes-2026-11-18, tracked), and NAR's October Pending Home Sales Index prints 10:00 the same morning per its own 2026 schedule. Whether a 14:00 minutes release compresses the morning the way a 14:00 SEP decision does (SPY 10:00 hour 26.0% of session range vs 40.4% baseline) is UNMEASURED — this session did not test it and the initial research should, because it is the difference between two grades of confounding rather than a repeat of one. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the inertness this session re-derived for the neighbouring EHS class (123 release days since 2016: ITB 1.927% median session range vs a 1.840% baseline, p=0.32); whether homebuilders are inert on a STARTS/PERMITS print is a separate question nobody here has measured. Distinct from the already-proposed housing-starts-2026-12-17, which is the NOVEMBER reference month and a funding-cliff test; this one is October's and a nowcast-channel test. One class considered and DECLINED so its absence reads as a decision: NAR's October Pending Home Sales Index on 2026-11-18, which the sibling lane already declined on the record as a routine monthly edition — the same criterion applies here and nothing this session measured changes it. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
